primitives.verbatim_quote: We use two primary models: 1) a Completion Probability (CP) model, which estimates the probability of a throw being successfully completed at any given target location, and 2) a Field Value (FV) model, which assigns positional value on the field as measured by scoring probability.

reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational operators—Completion Probability (CP) and Field Value (FV)—are constructed from high-dimensional spatial and temporal data. CP models the conditional probability of a successful throw given thrower and receiver locations, incorporating game time. FV maps field positions to expected scoring probabilities. These models are combined into a Player Contribution Metric (PCM), which aggregates individual throw contributions weighted by contextual relevance. The CP model assumes logistic dependency on spatial features, while FV encodes static positional utility. PCM synthesizes both into a scalar metric for comparative player analysis. Dualities emerge in how CP emphasizes dynamic execution and FV emphasizes strategic positioning. Failure modes include overfitting to rare events, misalignment of feature importance, and lack of temporal coherence in game state transitions. The framework supports retroactive and prospective evaluation of player decisions, enabling GSI to compute posterior belief updates and GSE to simulate alternative tactical paths.
